subject.title: Feature: configurable /new greeting model (or option to suppress greeting)

question: What public reset-greeting contract should OpenClaw support for bare `/new` and `/reset`: static ack, model greeting, suppressible ack, model override, or a typed combination?
rationale: Current main intentionally avoids model cost, related reports request restoring the persona greeting, and adding a config/model-routing surface is compatibility-sensitive product policy rather than a narrow repair.

options.title: Define a typed reset-greeting policy
options.body: Add one cross-surface config contract that preserves a safe default while allowing explicit model greeting, static ack/suppression, and optional cheaper model routing with docs and focused tests.

options.title: Keep static acknowledgements only
options.body: Close the configurable greeting direction and treat current no-model reset acknowledgement as the supported product behavior, leaving greeting users to send a post-reset message.

options.title: Restore greeting fallthrough by default
options.body: Return to the historical model turn for bare resets and require a separate suppression path, accepting the token-cost and upgrade implications for current users.

recommendation.title: Define a typed reset-greeting policy
recommendation.body: Add one cross-surface config contract that preserves a safe default while allowing explicit model greeting, static ack/suppression, and optional cheaper model routing with docs and focused tests.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored the current static acknowledgement behavior and the previous review framing this as an unresolved reset-greeting product decision.
